name: Bang Bang Chicken Bowls

ingredients.buy: to taste (about 2 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp ground black pepper)
1 tbsp plus 1/2 tsp, or more to taste
6 cups shredded (about half a medium head)
2 medium onions, thinly sliced and quick-pickled

writer_notes: All prose numbers taken only from the locked view: 14 servings, 588 cal, 44.7g protein, 59.8g carbs, 18.9g fat, prep PT15M. No number computed.

prose.intro_html:
Bang bang chicken usually shows up deep fried, drowned in a creamy sauce, and priced like a night out. We are going to keep the flavor and lose the deep fryer, because your wallet and your arteries both deserve a break. This is a meal-prep bowl built around lean chicken breast, a two-rice base, and a sauce that punches way above what it costs to make.

Here is the headline. Each of these 14 bowls lands at 588 calories with 44.7 grams of protein, 59.8 grams of carbs, and 18.9 grams of fat. That is a full, sauced, topping-loaded dinner that still clears 40 grams of protein without breaking a sweat. Prep runs about 15 minutes of hands-on work. You cook once and you eat like this all week.
prose.shop_smart:
The sauce is where the flavor lives and it is almost entirely pantry stuff. Light mayonnaise, sweet chili sauce, ketchup, sriracha, and garlic powder are shelf-stable staples you keep on hand, and a batch this size uses 2 2/3 cups of mayo and 1 3/4 cups of sweet chili sauce, so buy the standard jars, not the little squeeze bottles. The powdered peanut butter, PB2, is the one item people skip because they think it is fancy. It is not. One jar of that powder lasts many batches, so 3 1/2 tablespoons here barely dents it.

On the base, buy plain long-grain white rice and cook 7 cups from about 2 1/3 cups dry. Cheaper than any microwave pouch, every time. The frozen riced cauliflower does the same job as fresh for a fraction of the fuss, and 2 3/4 pounds cooks straight from the bag. For the toppings, buy whole and cut it yourself: a medium head of cabbage gives you the 6 cups you need with plenty left over, five medium carrots julienne down to 3 cups, and two yellow onions quick-pickle in the time it takes the chicken to cook. Whole vegetables shredded at home always beat the pre-cut trays on value.
prose.make_it:
Start the chicken. Heat a large skillet over medium heat with the olive oil, add the cubed chicken breast, and season with the salt and black pepper. Let it cook untouched for 3 minutes so it browns, then flip and repeat until the pieces are cooked through and no longer pink. Do not crowd the pan, and if 5 1/4 pounds is too much for one skillet, work in two batches.

While the chicken cooks, mix the sauce. Whisk together the light mayonnaise, sweet chili sauce, ketchup, sriracha, garlic powder, and the powdered peanut butter until it is smooth and fully combined. Taste it and add more sriracha if you want it hotter.

When the chicken is done, turn off the heat and stir about a third of the sauce into the pan to coat it. Save the rest to drizzle on the finished bowls, because a sauced bowl beats a dry one every time.

Build the bowls. Combine the cooked white rice and the cooked cauliflower rice and split that base across your containers. Pile on the shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, sliced cucumber, and quick-pickled onions, then add a portion of the sauced chicken. Drizzle the reserved sauce over the top and finish with chopped green onions and the toasted sesame seeds.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers. The honest way to split it even is to weigh, not eyeball. Combine the two rices, then divide the base by weight across the 14 bowls so nobody gets shorted. Do the same with the chicken: total pan weight divided by 14, straight down the line.

The sauce splits two ways. Most of it is already stirred into the chicken; the reserve gets drizzled evenly over the top, roughly a spoonful per bowl. Toppings are the flexible part, so distribute the cabbage, carrots, cucumber, pickled onion, green onion, and sesame seeds by eye. Every container comes out at that same 588 calories and 44.7 grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is the math that matters. This whole build comes out to {{cost_ps}} per serving, and for that you get a sauced, protein-packed, topping-loaded bowl that a restaurant would charge you ten times over for and still serve smaller. Cook it once, eat it 14 times, and the per-bowl number is the only one your budget feels.
prose.upsell_html: If bowls like this are how you want to eat every week without guessing at the numbers, that is the whole point of Thrifty Crew. Membership is a dollar a month, and it gets you every recipe costed and macro'd exactly like this one. Cook smart, spend less, eat better.

head.description: Meal-prep Bang Bang Chicken Bowls: lean chicken breast, a white rice and cauliflower rice base, crunchy toppings, and a creamy sweet-heat sauce. 14 servings at 588 calories and 44.7g protein each.

When the chicken is fully cooked, turn off the heat and stir about a third of the sauce into the pan to coat the chicken. Reserve the rest to drizzle on the finished bowls.

Combine the cooked white rice and cooked cauliflower rice and split the base across the containers. Top with shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, sliced cucumber, and quick-pickled onions, add the sauced chicken, drizzle with reserved sauce, and finish with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
